engagement_background.objective: Identify and implement $678K–$1.65M of annual cost savings (≈8% of a $18–36M baseline) by leveraging Epika’s enterprise-wide purchasing power, improving supplier agreements, and accelerating value creation ahead of Trivest Partners’ planned exit.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Strategic sourcing across 13 spend categories (OEM, Aftermarket Parts, Oil/Lubes, Filters, Employee Benefits, P-Card, Fuel, Telecom, General Industrial Supplies, Tires, Uniforms, Waste, Office Supplies) representing ~$51.9M in annual spend of which ~$36.2M is addressable; project to run in ‘Fast-Track’, Wave 1, and Wave 2 phases with completion targeted for February 2025.
constraints_challenges: Highly decentralized procurement – 8 autonomous business units with separate systems and practices.
Minimal internal spend data; Treya had to request line-item history directly from suppliers to build 80% of the baseline.
Aggressive six-month timeline driven by PE sponsor’s planned sale within 6–7 months of kickoff.
Long-standing incumbent supplier relationships not previously leveraged at an enterprise level, creating negotiation sensitivities.
Supplier non-responsiveness to data requests and potential pushback during negotiations.
Limited bandwidth of Epika stakeholders to support data gathering and decision making.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Little in-house purchasing data; spend details scattered across multiple technology platforms for each business unit. Detailed line-item data obtained primarily from high-spend suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No consolidated spend view, inconsistent formats across business units, significant gaps until suppliers provided records.
